about: Case file CF6 (cf6-shifting-load-to-clean-hours), wave W2 draft, 2026-11-03. 'timeline' and 'boundary' describe a published study by the course author (Li et al. 2025), drawn from approved excerpts (reports/learn/excerpts_for_approval.md, E6); the paper's date is the publisher's date on Crossref (accessed 3 Nov 2026). 'idea' uses Prairie Town (fictional; plants, sizes and CO2 rates illustrative, from town.json) on the real shapes of 9 June 2025 on the Southwest Power Pool grid (EIA-930, town_year.json), the day lesson 9 uses, scaled the same way. Each hour is dispatched cheapest first as in lesson 9 (no ramp limits, no minimum output): the town's 100 MW zero-carbon plant runs flat, then wind and sun, then the combined-cycle plant, then the peaker; a negative gap is spilled wind and sun.

events.label: The data year
events.text: Hourly demand and generation by fuel for U.S. grid regions, from EIA's hourly grid data.

events.label: Paper published
events.text: Load re-timed by hourly average emission intensity in U.S. grid regions, with windows of a month, a quarter or a year.

source.label: Li et al. (2025), Cell Reports Sustainability 2, 100367

events.label: Model framework released
events.text: A documented, open implementation of the load-regulation model, with synthetic example regions (version 1.0.0).

boundary.title: Where the study's result holds
boundary.lede: The reductions are an accounting result within the study's stated boundary:
holds: emissions are counted at each hour's [[average-emission-factor|average]] intensity;
each window is known in advance (perfect foresight);
each window's total use does not fall;
hourly EIA data for U.S. grid regions in 2023.
leaves: the grid's consequential response: which plants actually change output (the [[marginal-emission-factor|marginal]] view);
the cost of moving load, apart from a penalty on each adjusted hour.
boundary.source: From the approved excerpt of Li et al. (2025), Cell Reports Sustainability.

idea.title: Move 10 MWh in Prairie Town's day
idea.note: Prairie Town is illustrative: its plants and CO₂ rates are invented; the hourly shapes are real (9 June 2025, Southwest Power Pool).

facts.what: Reduction in attributed emissions in grids with diverse generation when the adjustment range widened from ±5% to ±8% of each hour's load.
facts.source: Li et al. (2025), Cell Reports Sustainability

facts.n: one to two percent or less
facts.what: The order of the reductions in the reported scenarios, as a share of regional totals.
facts.source: Li et al. (2025), Cell Reports Sustainability
